mustFix.title: The draft is a fourth review turn in a three-turn protocol; D-000 clause 2 mandates CONTESTED, and the corpus forbids a turn 4 in terms
mustFix.where: line 5: '> **Protocol:** D-000 new cycle, turn 4 of 3.'
mustFix.measurement: D-272's review history is turn 1 Split (Claude CONSENT 0/0, Codex OBJECT CODEX-D272-SF1), turn 2 Dual OBJECT, turn 3 Dual OBJECT — three exchanges per party with no consensus at any turn. Across all 340 COORD drafts in docs/coop/artifacts/, 'turn N of 3' resolves to: 236x 'turn 1 of 3', 79x 'turn 2 of 3', 24x 'turn 3 of 3', and exactly 1x 'turn 4 of 3' — this subject. It is the only fourth-turn draft in the corpus. The subject never mentions CONTESTED, D-000 clause 2, parking, or batching (grep -iE 'contested|clause 2|parked|batch' returns nothing).
mustFix.authority: D-000 clause 2, COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md lines 32-36: '**Termination clause: 3 turns each side.** If no consensus after three exchanges per party, the decision is recorded `CONTESTED` with both positions, parked, and batched to the user; work proceeds on other surfaces. A forced consensus is never recorded as consensus.' The status vocabulary at line 15 confirms: `CONTESTED` = 'no consensus after 3 turns each; parked for the user'.
mustFix.precedent: The corpus refuses a fourth turn in terms, repeatedly and without exception. D-017/D-019-D-024 (line 1493): 'CONTESTED after three turns under D-000 clause 2. Not adopted. No forced consensus. Parked. Successor drafts are D-025-D-031, a **new** cycle, not a fourth turn of this one.' D-059 (line 2487): 'A later new cycle (not turn 4 of this cycle) may retry.' D-064 (line 2507), the successor to CONTESTED D-059: 'New cycle after CONTESTED D-059. Not a fourth turn.' — and it opens at '**Turn 1 of 3**', under a new decision id. Same idiom at lines 2659, 2751, 3764, 3795. The single case in the corpus of a fourth review round, D-093 (line 3695), was deliberately NOT numbered turn 4: 'Turn 3 of 3, re-dispatched after a freeze-digest mismatch (not a fourth turn; the first turn-3 verdicts were freeze-precondition OBJECTs, not merits reviews)'.
mustFix.why: The D-093 escape hatch is the only sanctioned route to a fourth review round, and it is unavailable here on the facts: D-272's turn-3 verdicts were merits reviews, not freeze-precondition OBJECTs. Claude turn 3 was OBJECT 1 MUST-FIX / 3 SHOULD-FIX on the substance of the entry, and Codex turn 3 was OBJECT CODEX-D272-T3-MF1 / CODEX-D272-T3-SF1 on the substance. Three merits exchanges closed without consensus, which is exactly the condition clause 2 addresses. Adopting a CONSENT reached at a fourth turn would record as consensus a result the protocol says must be recorded as CONTESTED — the 'forced consensus' clause 2 names and forbids. The defect is not cosmetic numbering: it goes to whether this draft may exist at all, and it is invisible on the face of the entry because the subject cites no authority for the extension and never names the clause it is operating past. Note also that line 5 is internally self-refuting on its own terms — 'new cycle' and 'turn 4 of 3' are mutually exclusive under D-064, where a new cycle takes a new decision id and opens at turn 1 of 3. This entry is numbered D-272 throughout and recites turns 1-3 of D-272 as its own prior turns, so it is plainly the same cycle, not a new one.
mustFix.remedy: Take one of the two lawful routes. (a) Record D-272 `CONTESTED` under D-000 clause 2 with both positions preserved, park it, and batch to the user; a later new cycle under a fresh decision id may retry the same recording, opening at 'turn 1 of 3' on the D-064 model. Or (b) if the coordinator holds that some turn-3 verdict was a freeze-precondition OBJECT rather than a merits review — which this reviewer does not find on the record — re-dispatch explicitly as 'turn 3 of 3, re-dispatched', citing D-093 and stating the ground, rather than incrementing past the bound. Either way, do not adopt an entry whose face reads 'turn 4 of 3' with no cited authority. Invent no identifiers.

shouldFix.title: Bare Claude finding identifiers collide across turns: MF-1, SF-1 and SF-2 each denote two different findings in the same document, with no turn qualifier
shouldFix.measurement: Line 225 'This turn 4 lands CODEX-D272-T3-MF1 and MF-1 (same class)' uses MF-1 for the turn-3 finding (Stage B turn 2 disposition). Line 236 'This turn 3 landing of MF-1 remains' uses MF-1 for the turn-2 finding (Stage B turn 1 disposition). These are different findings sharing one string, eleven lines apart in one paragraph. Same collision for SF-1: line 5 'CODEX-D272-T3-SF1 / SF-1 / SF-2 (same class)' means the turn-3 SF-1, while lines 84, 232 and 242 ('CODEX-D272-T2-SF1 is the same class as SF-1', 'This turn 3 lands SF-1') mean the turn-2 SF-1. Same for SF-2 (line 5 turn-3; lines 231, 243 turn-2).
shouldFix.contrast: Codex identifiers in this same document are turn-namespaced and therefore collision-free: CODEX-D272-SF1 (turn 1), CODEX-D272-T2-SF1 (turn 2), CODEX-D272-T3-MF1 and CODEX-D272-T3-SF1 (turn 3). The subject reproduces all four correctly and never confuses them. Only the Claude side is bare.
shouldFix.why: This entry's entire subject matter is exact identifier accounting — it devotes lines 87-106 to dispositioning observation identifiers precisely and states at lines 218-221 that it 'does not invent a Codex identifier' and 'does not claim that both reviewers' identifiers are preserved'. A record that polices identifier precision that carefully should not leave its own finding identifiers ambiguous. On adoption, a reader tracing 'MF-1' through the COORD entry cannot resolve which finding is meant without reconstructing turn order from surrounding prose. This was tolerable while each draft recited one prior turn; at four turns reciting three prior rounds it is a genuine ambiguity in the record, and it compounds the more turns accumulate.
shouldFix.remedy: Qualify the Claude identifiers by turn wherever more than one round is recited — e.g. 'turn-2 MF-1' and 'turn-3 MF-1', or adopt the Codex-style namespace already in use in this document. Do not renumber or invent identifiers; qualify the existing ones in prose only.

decisionRule: CONSENT only if no MUST-FIX and no SHOULD-FIX.
summary: OBJECT at 1 MUST-FIX and 2 SHOULD-FIX. The dispatched work is done and done well: the subject is byte-exact at 802ca3ec... mode 0444 on D-271 HEAD, all 19 measured inputs reproduce, and all six dispatched identifiers are substantively landed — the Stage B turn 2 verdict table, the Stage B turn 2 observation disposition, the turn-2 posture prose, the explicit frozen turn-2 draft path with its 'not a sibling .turn2.draft.md' disclaimer, and standalone 'stays unmoved' clauses for all three prior turn drafts. Every fact claim survived attack: DR-118 DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED, DR-125 OPEN and DR-107 PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW all match live file 08, required-now 28 of 28, owners 32 of 32, DR-G32 last, the Stage A and Stage B observation shapes are reproduced exactly with no invented Codex identifier and no recasting of Codex's absent observations field as an empty list, leftover-join.v3 correctly current at draft time, v4 not current and not Dual ACCEPT, sdk v6 current, and the D-236-skipping branch enumeration correct. What fails is not the content of the turn but the existence of it. D-000 clause 2 is a termination clause: three turns each side, and if no consensus, the decision is recorded CONTESTED, parked, and batched to the user, because 'a forced consensus is never recorded as consensus'. D-272 ran Split, then Dual OBJECT, then Dual OBJECT — three exchanges, no consensus — so clause 2 is already engaged. 'turn 4 of 3' appears exactly once in 340 corpus drafts, here; and the corpus refuses a fourth turn in terms five separate times, most pointedly at D-064, which followed CONTESTED D-059 as a 'New cycle... Not a fourth turn' opening at turn 1 of 3 under a new decision id. The one fourth review round the corpus does contain, D-093, was expressly labeled 'not a fourth turn' on the ground that the earlier turn-3 verdicts were freeze-precondition OBJECTs rather than merits reviews — a ground unavailable here, since both turn-3 verdicts were merits OBJECTs. Record D-272 CONTESTED, or re-open under a new decision id at turn 1 of 3; do not adopt an entry whose face reads 'turn 4 of 3' with no cited authority. The two SHOULD-FIXes are identifier hygiene in an entry whose whole subject is identifier precision: the bare Claude identifiers MF-1/SF-1/SF-2 each carry two meanings, and the Decision section never states that this turn lands the turn-3 SF-1 or SF-2.
